title: Royal Bank of Canada's athlete showcase - SportsAid Week 2016
description: Paralympic heroes Ellie Simmonds, Pam Relph and Toby Gold reflected on the importance of the support they received from SportsAid as they met young athletes currently being helped by the charity at the Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) offices in London during the inaugural SportsAid Week. RBC, a key partner of SportsAid since 2013, hosted a special athlete showcase for staff at its Thames Court and Riverbank House offices with demonstrations provided on boxing, modern pentathlon, judo and rhythmic gymnastics.

asr.full_text: We're at RBC's office today, we've been at both of their offices, Thames Court and. Riverbank House and we're here to celebrate Sports Aid Week and mainly to. Celebrate the partnership with RBC which has been amazing. They're really. Interested in helping athletes, that seems to be in their DNA, they've got lots of. Energy that really is rubbing off on the partnership. Today we've brought six. Sports into their offices and what we've brought together is an exciting day of. Of interaction with young athletes. Chance to actually see them in their sweet spot. Just brings the story alive. It's been great. It's been great to see the athletes. Been great to see the team from Sports Aid. And it's been really encouraging for us. To see so many employees being engaged throughout the day. Sports Aid Week appeals to the staff. Because it's a combination of sporting athletes,. Which a lot of people are very interested in,. But also young athletes. It hits a lot of the right buttons. And the charity itself does a fantastic job. Of translating that money and the fundraising into genuine benefits for the athletes themselves. I've had so much fun today being involved in the Sports Aid week. We're just trying. To get the message across about fundraising and what Sports Aid do. For me it helped me. Start my career, it helped me get into my sport and it's helped for the future and the. Legacy of British sport. Sports Aid have been a major help, RBC has been a major help. If Sports Aid didn't help. Me then I would try and struggle and find a way but the fact that they've. Made it easier is the biggest thing. The fact that SportsAid has taken that stress. Off the athlete to focus more on the sport adds to the performance. Less stress. Better performance and that's what SportsAid and RBC have done. Today is. Obviously a very important day during the year really focusing on SportsAid. But it is it is a relationship and a partnership which continues throughout. The year. We have a buddy scheme which some of our staff been engaged in. Supporting some of the athletes and giving them some mentoring and some. Advice and we also invited teams from SportsAid to participate in some of our. Events so it's very much a mutual partnership and as I said we keep the. Momentum going throughout throughout this year and beyond. The buddy scheme is great because it means I get to check in with Paul, tell him about how I'm. Progressing with my uni, with my athletics, it's kind of like having a touch base and. Getting advice from him as well which has been really really useful. It's a real opportunity for me to get involved in something which is really inspirational,. But also to try and pass on some knowledge and some advice to Imani. Will excels at a sport that I would love to excel at. Unfortunately I don't. All I can offer him is. My friendship and a point of contact and if I can give Will any assistance or guidance whether it's. Regards to, I don't know, getting through school exams or, I don't know, talking about university,. I get loads from it. The success of SportsAid and my personal experience of it has really been about. Sharing in the enthusiasm that these people have as something that you can really then take with you in your day-to-day role. So they add as much as RBC gives financially, we get much more I think in return. Having seen how well our younger generation have done over the last few years,. Particularly at the London Olympics and now in Rio,. We've really seen the performance of Team GB and to have obviously the benefit of a fantastic charity like SportsAid behind them. Has really I think inspired the whole country. It's certainly a great charity for us to be involved and partner with at RBC. And so I couldn't recommend it more in terms of inspiring people both in the workforce but really to see how we're supporting that younger generation come through. In general, SportsAid is trying to find supporters to support our work. You'd imagine that. But particularly commercial partners bring a little bit extra to the pot. It's not only their cash commitment, but they've got a whole office space full of professional people. And what that allows us to do is connect that professionalism, if you like, the world of work,. To these young athletes who are embarking on a career in sport. And if we can bring the two together, there's a lot of value out there. Add there so it seems like a perfect mix and this is a really good example of that with RBC.
